messages.content: Can you retrieve the weather forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function requests_get with appropriate params. The user wants forecast for White Plains next week with temperatures in Celsius. We need to get coordinates for White Plains. White Plains is a city in New York, USA. Coordinates approx: latitude 41.0536° N, longitude -73.7629° W. So latitude=41.0536, longitude=-73.7629. For forecast, we can use Open-Meteo API. The endpoint likely is "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". We need to specify parameters: latitude, longitude, daily variables like temperature_2m_max, temperature_2m_min, etc. Also set timezone. For next week, we need start_date and end_date. Today is unknown but we can set start_date as tomorrow. But we don't know current date. We can approximate using today's date. Let's assume today is 2026-07-28. Next week would be 2026-07-29 to 2026-08-04. We'll set start_date=2026-07-29, end_date=2026-08-04. Also set daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min. And set temperature_unit=celsius. Actually Open-Meteo uses "temperature_unit" param. Also "timezone" param. We'll set timezone=America/New_York. So function call:

{
  url: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast",
  params: {
    latitude: 41.0536,
    longitude: -73.7629,
    daily: ["temperature_2m_max", "temperature_2m_min"],
    start_date: "2026-07-29",
    end_date: "2026-08-04",
    timezone: "America/New_York",
    temperature_unit: "celsius"
  }
}

But the function signature expects params as an object with keys: latitude, longitude, elevation. It doesn't mention daily, start_date, etc. However the description says "Query parameters for the GET request." It lists only latitude, longitude, elevation. But maybe it's incomplete. In practice, we can pass additional query parameters. The function signature may allow arbitrary keys. We'll pass them anyway.

Thus we call the function.
